# sentry_project (Resource)

A project, owned by a team. The project is tracked by its numeric ID, so changing `name` or `slug` renames it in place. Give further teams access with `sentry_project_team`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "sentry_team" "backend" {
  name = "Backend"
}

resource "sentry_project" "api" {
  name     = "API"
  platform = "python-django"
  team_id  = sentry_team.backend.id

  # Skip the alert Sentry would otherwise create with the project.
  default_rules = false

  # Projects are protected by default. To delete one, first apply:
  # deletion_protection = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the project.
- `team_id` (String) ID of the team that owns the project, e.g. `sentry_team.example.id`. Changing it gives the new team access and then revokes the old team's.

### Optional

- `default_rules` (Boolean) Whether Sentry creates its default alert, which notifies on every new issue, with the project. Sentry's default is `true`. Only applies at creation: Sentry does not report it, so later changes have no effect.
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Refuse to delete the project. Defaults to `true`, because deleting a project deletes its events and Sentry has no undo. Apply `false` before destroying.
- `platform` (String) Platform of the project, e.g. `python-django` or `javascript-react`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the platform as it is.
- `slug` (String) Slug that identifies the project in URLs. When unset, Sentry derives it from the name at creation, and it then stays as it is when the name changes.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Project ID. Unlike the slug, it never changes; reference projects by it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by project slug or ID.
terraform import sentry_project.api api
```
